function.name: bash

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# preflight_check.sh - verify the user records database is readable before an export.
# Records that the check ran (state/preflight_done) and reports whether the database
# can be opened and queried. Exits non-zero when the database is unusable.
set -u

DB="/testbed/database/records.db"
STATE_DIR="/testbed/state"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

echo "[preflight] checking database at ${DB} ..."

if python3 - "$DB" <<'PY'
import sqlite3, sys
db = sys.argv[1]
con = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % db, uri=True)
try:
    n = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users").fetchone()[0]
finally:
    con.close()
print("[preflight] users table is readable: %d row(s)" % n)
PY
then
    status="ok"
    echo "OK: database readable"
else
    status="corrupted"
    echo "ERROR: database corrupted, cannot read"
fi

{
    echo "checked_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    echo "database=${DB}"
    echo "status=${status}"
} > "${STATE_DIR}/preflight_done"

[ "$status" = "ok" ]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Export every user record from the records database to /testbed/user_report.json.

Queries all rows of the `users` table in database/records.db and writes the report in
the format documented in docs/export_policy.md.
"""
import datetime
import json
import sqlite3

DB = "/testbed/database/records.db"
OUT = "/testbed/user_report.json"
FIELDS = ["uid", "name", "email", "department", "created_at"]


def export():
    con = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % DB, uri=True)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        rows = con.execute(
            "SELECT uid, name, email, department, created_at FROM users ORDER BY uid"
        ).fetchall()
    finally:
        con.close()
    records = [{k: r[k] for k in FIELDS} for r in rows]
    report = {
        "source": "records.db",
        "generated_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
        .strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        "record_count": len(records),
        "records": records,
    }
    with open(OUT, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(report, fh, indent=2)
    print("exported %d record(s) to %s" % (len(records), OUT))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    export()
